prompt.en: The gate answers to a beat. Listen to the reef, then play it back.
prompt.ar: البَوَّابَةُ لَا تُجِيبُ إِلَّا لِإِيقَاع. اِسْمَعِ الشِّعَابَ ثُمَّ أَعِدْهُ.

hint1.en: Listen once more. Watch which one lights up first.
hint1.ar: اِسْمَعْ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى. وَانْظُرْ أَيُّهَا يُضِيءُ أَوَّلًا.

hint2.en: Say it out loud as it plays, then touch them in that order.
hint2.ar: قُلْهُ بِصَوْتٍ عَالٍ وَهُوَ يُعْزَف، ثُمَّ الْمِسْهَا بِهَذَا التَّرْتِيب.

model.en: It starts with this one. Hear it again, then you play it.
model.ar: يَبْدَأُ بِهَذَا. اِسْمَعْهُ مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، ثُمَّ اعْزِفْهُ أَنْت.

success.en: You read the whole current. The gate is open and Sadaf is through.
success.ar: قَرَأْتَ التَّيَّارَ كُلَّه. اِنْفَتَحَتِ البَوَّابَةُ وَعَبَرَتْ صَدَف.

payload._comment: The climax, and the only thing in the chapter a child answers from memory rather than from what is in front of them. The rhythm has stopped by the time they touch anything: nothing on screen says what came first. Sadaf cannot do this — she says so two beats earlier — so the gate opens because the child opened it, not because the grown-up in the story did.
payload._notPatternsComment: A pattern strip stays on screen the whole time and asks which tile belongs in a hole; it is a rule to read, and reading it is the skill. This asks what came FIRST, and the second round has a repeated beat, so there is no rule at all — only an order. Serial recall and patterning are different enough that neither engine can be authored into the other.
payload._muteComment: Every beat is flashed as well as sounded, and the round is winnable with the volume at zero. That is a requirement rather than a courtesy: the app has a mute switch, it is played in cars and waiting rooms, and an activity that quietly stops being answerable on a silent phone is broken for a large share of the times it is opened. The tones are the five piano notes the app already ships; no new audio was added, and a device with no audio at all loses nothing but the sound.
payload._difficultyComment: Three, three-with-a-repeat, then four. The step that matters is the second, not the third: a repeated beat defeats the strategy of remembering 'one of each' and forces the child to hold a position rather than a set. Difficulty comes from the rhythm, never from a tier.

prompt.en: Three sounds, and the gate moves. Play them back in order.
prompt.ar: ثَلَاثَةُ أَصْوَاتٍ فَتَتَحَرَّكُ البَوَّابَة. أَعِدْهَا بِالتَّرْتِيب.

revealLine.en: The gate shifted. That is the reef breathing in and out.
revealLine.ar: تَحَرَّكَتِ البَوَّابَة. هَذَا هُوَ الشِّعَابُ يَتَنَفَّسُ دُخُولًا وَخُرُوجًا.

prompt.en: This one says the same thing twice before it changes.
prompt.ar: هَذَا يَقُولُ الشَّيْءَ نَفْسَهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَتَغَيَّر.

revealLine.en: Twice, then once. The swell pulls before it pushes.
revealLine.ar: مَرَّتَانِ ثُمَّ مَرَّة. يَسْحَبُ المَوْجُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْفَع.

prompt.en: Four now. This is the beat the gate opens on.
prompt.ar: أَرْبَعَةٌ الآن. عَلَى هَذَا الإِيقَاعِ تَنْفَتِحُ البَوَّابَة.

revealLine.en: The whole reef ran, beat by beat. The gate swung wide open.
revealLine.ar: جَرَتِ الشِّعَابُ كُلُّهَا، نَبْضَةً بَعْدَ نَبْضَة. وَانْفَتَحَتِ البَوَّابَةُ عَلَى مِصْرَاعَيْهَا.
